_note: Verified facts only, from Jack's transaction emails and Compass records (see claude/city-sales-facts in the project). side = which side Jack represented.

sales.title: Under contract in ten days, $20,000 gained in the counter
sales.story: A three bedroom rambler near Lake Hills Park. An inspection was done before it went on the market so buyers could see the condition up front, and the home was professionally photographed. Offers came in within the first ten days. The buyer opened at $1,170,000 and came up to $1,190,000 after my counter.

sales.title: Third offer, timed to the end of a lease
sales.story: My buyers wrote offers on two other homes this spring. One was too far apart on price, and on the other the seller took a different offer. For this Lakemont home they made a full price offer with the inspection waived and a 30 day close timed to the end of their lease. The seller accepted the next day.

sales.title: Over list, accepted in two days
sales.story: My buyers made an all cash offer $10,000 over the $1,075,000 list price, with no appraisal or financing contingency and the septic repairs waived. It was accepted about two days after the home was listed. The seller was represented by Stephen Macdonald, who I work alongside at the Macdonald Group.

bellevue.lead: Below are recent Bellevue sales where I represented the seller or the buyer, from a Lake Hills rambler to a Lakemont purchase, with what decided each one.
how: Pricing and negotiation decided the Bellevue sales. On the Lake Hills rambler, the buyer opened at $1,170,000 and my counter brought them to $1,190,000. For my Lakemont buyers, I put together price per square foot breakdowns from recent sales on the homes they considered, and they passed on one that was too far apart on price before winning the right one.
why: I've known these neighborhoods most of my life, so when I price a Bellevue home I'm comparing it to the streets around it, not a radius on a map. I'm a second generation broker, and I handle the comps, the counteroffers and the calls with the other agent myself.

sales.title: Fix the one big item, keep the receipts
sales.story: The inspection before listing found a gas leak at the water heater. We had it fixed properly, kept the receipts for buyers, and handled the rest of the report: deck ledger, railings, garage fire wall and outlets.

photos.alt: White split level Kirkland home with black garage doors at dusk
Large lawn, patio and deck behind the Kirkland home

sales.title: Strong terms, accepted the same night
sales.story: The home was listed at $1,280,000. I sent my buyer the comps, the inspection report and the seller disclosure before we offered. After touring, they offered with the inspection and financing contingencies waived, earnest money released to the seller within two days, and a two week close. The seller countered and we agreed that evening at $1,255,000, $25,000 under list.
sales.result: $25,000 under list, accepted the same night

kirkland.lead: Below are two recent Kirkland sales, one where I was the listing agent and one where I represented the buyer, and the work that decided each.
how: In Kirkland, the deciding work happened before anyone wrote an offer. On the estate listing, the inspection before listing found the gas leak, and fixing it with receipts in hand meant buyers didn't have to guess. On the buyer side, my client had the comps, the inspection report and the seller disclosure before we wrote the offer, so they could make a strong one the same day they toured.
why: Most of the trouble in a sale shows up in the inspection. When it makes sense, I have the house inspected before it's listed, so we fix what matters, keep the receipts, and hand buyers the reports up front. Fewer surprises after an offer means fewer fights over price.

sales.title: A $4.8 million listing, negotiated to $4.6 million
sales.story: A new construction home with a bonus room over the garage and a detached cottage, listed at $4,800,000. My buyers opened with a cash offer and a written valuation that broke out the main house, the garage and bonus room, and the cottage separately. I compared the seller's comparables with recent Redmond luxury sales, and after several days of back and forth we agreed at $4,600,000, $200,000 under list.

sales.title: A remodel buyers could finally see
sales.story: A 2023 remodel had already redone the kitchen, both bathrooms, flooring, windows, doors and electrical, but the outside hid it. We put in a new lawn and garden bed, added parking and repainted, and I wrote a "What's new" flyer from the contractor's invoice so buyers could see every update. One showing, one full price offer within a day, inspection waived.

photos.alt: Redmond rambler with new lawn, garden bed and fresh exterior paint
Fenced backyard with patio and new lawn

sales.note: Part of an estate sale. The final price reflects a $6,000 adjustment two days before closing, in place of a credit the buyer's lender couldn't allow.
sales.result: Full price offer within a day

sales.title: Fix what worries buyers, skip the rest
sales.story: Part of an estate sale. I went through the inspection report and picked only what was likely to worry a buyer: electrical, small plumbing leaks and a capped vent. Each fix was keyed to the report so buyers could see it was handled.

redmond.lead: My recent Redmond sales range from a $1.27 million rambler to a $4.6 million new construction purchase. Each one below shows how the price was set and negotiated.
how: Redmond homes range widely in price, so the valuation has to hold up. On the $4.6 million purchase, the opening offer came with a written valuation that priced the main house, the garage and bonus room, and the cottage separately, and I checked the seller's comparables against recent Redmond luxury sales. The two Redmond estate listings needed opposite plans: one needed curb appeal, the other only the repairs a buyer would worry about.
why: This year I've represented Redmond sellers and a Redmond buyer, from a $1.27 million rambler to a $4.6 million new construction home. Working both sides keeps me honest about what buyers will question, and I write the marketing to answer it. On the rambler below, that meant turning a contractor's invoice into a flyer, because buyers can't see a remodel in a photo.

sales.title: Prepared, staged and documented
sales.story: Before listing, the sellers painted the interior, refinished the hardwoods and washed the exterior. I recommended staging, and the home was professionally photographed, including drone views. Septic repairs were completed and documented before closing so the buyers had a clean report.

sales.title: Staged condo, sold through the holidays
sales.story: A condo in the Sammamish Hills community. I recommended professional staging, and it was staged and photographed before listing. It went under contract on December 24 after about two months on the market.

sales.title: Back on market, won with a rent back
sales.story: This Hamptons Pointe condo went pending with another buyer, then came back on the market. My counter offered the sellers a four week rent back, and the offer was accepted two days later. I also confirmed with the HOA what the dues cover, since the listing details conflicted.
sales.result: Won with a four week rent back

sales.title: Condo purchase, credit negotiated after inspection
sales.story: I sent my buyer comps and the HOA documents before we offered on this Sammamish Pointe condo. After the inspection we negotiated a credit, the appraisal came in at value, and it closed at $480,000, $5,000 under list.
sales.result: $5,000 under list plus a repair credit

issaquah.lead: I've sold Issaquah homes and condos and helped buyers purchase here, from a Sycamore single family home to condos in Sammamish Hills, Sammamish Pointe and Hamptons Pointe.
how: Issaquah buyers compare carefully. On both listings below I recommended professional staging, and on the Sycamore home the septic repairs were documented before closing. On the buyer side, when a listing's HOA details conflicted, I checked directly with the HOA before my clients committed.
why: Condo and HOA communities are a big part of Issaquah, and the paperwork is where those sales go sideways. I get the HOA documents in front of buyers early and check anything that doesn't add up, so a deal doesn't stall in escrow over something nobody read.

sales.title: Twilight photos and a timely price adjustment
sales.story: I had twilight photos taken and used them as the lead listing images, and shared the inspection report from before listing with buyers, including a roof vent leak that had already been sealed. In late June I recommended a price adjustment, and an offer came in three days later. The sellers accepted it that day.
sales.result: Offer three days after the price adjustment

sammamish.lead: One recent Sammamish listing below shows how presentation and a price adjustment brought a buyer, and how I approach selling on the plateau.
how: With more homes for buyers to choose from, presentation and pricing carry a lot of weight in Sammamish. On this Trossachs listing I used twilight photos as the lead images and gave buyers the inspection report from before listing. In late June I recommended a price adjustment, and an offer came in three days later.
why: Sammamish buyers often have plenty of homes to compare, so how a listing looks online decides who comes to see it. I order the photography myself and decide which shots lead, and I give buyers the inspection reports up front so nobody is guessing.
